title: What makes an AI narrative game FEEL alive? [Looking for feedback]
author: Wild_Juggernaut_7913
selftext:
I've been working on a side project for the past 6 months - an AI-powered narrative game where characters actually remember your conversations and evolve over time.

I'm curious though - what elements make interactive stories engaging for you?

Is it:

\- Characters that have distinct personalities?

\- Choices that actually change the story?

\- Being able to build relationships with AI characters?

\- Something else entirely?

For context, my project lets you explore different worlds (wasteland, sci-fi, fantasy) and interact through text/voice. The AI generates personalized responses on the fly.

But I'm much more interested in YOUR thoughts than pushing my project. What's your biggest pet peeve with AI games? What would make you want to keep playing?

Would love to hear this community's insights! 🎮

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Honestly very little so far. I'm in two betas for what I'd call the most "prod ready" ai rpgs and both of them are decently fun but ultimately still feel a bit more like dreaming about playing DND that actually doing it

replies.author: Wild_Juggernaut_7913
replies.body: What do you think is the most important thing to immerse players in the experience itself? We've made several teasers. If you're interested, I can share them with you. They show more plot content and interactive methods. Looking forward to deeper conversations with you

comments.author: dev-for-deco
comments.body: Nothing. Did you see some AI project with "soul"?
